note: Adapted from the species-level description of Emerson; original in English; soldier and worker present, alate not described; the worker is recorded only by antennal segment number and two measurements; figure numbers, localities and nest descriptions omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Mandible shape differs from that of M. brachignathus, so it is treated as a distinct species. Compared with the type material of M. secernens, the head is relatively longer and narrower and the mandibles shorter; the syntypes agree well, only the head being slightly narrower; M. solidus is also similar, its other type specimen having only a slightly shorter and wider head and slightly shorter mandibles. The head is wider than in M. parvus and proportionally longer. The specimen from Senegambina has a slightly longer head (2.50 mm) and is still treated as conspecific.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale red-yellow, proportionally long; sides straight and parallel. Antennae 13-segmented, the third segment shortest, the fourth almost as long as the second. Labrum pentagonal, sides straight. Mandibles relatively short, with short serrations. Anterior margin of the pronotum usually distinctly notched, but one specimen from Poko shows no notch, while another soldier in the same vial is notched. Head length (with mandibles) 2.16–2.40 mm; head length (to the apex of the labrum) 1.83–1.90 mm; head length (to the antennal bases) 1.40–1.43 mm; head width 0.87–0.89 mm; antennal length 1.16–1.17 mm; pronotum length 0.35 mm, width 0.53–0.57 mm; hind tibia length 0.70–0.73 mm; left mandible length 0.90–0.94 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Only antennae 13-segmented are recorded, together with two measurements, head width and hind tibia length (given in the original as .92 mm and .56 mm); no other characters are described.
